Rising AppalachiaIn Appalachia, farmers still practice the ancestral tradition of companion planting. Corn grows tall as a trellis, beans climb the corn, and squash provides the ground cover. Rising Appalachia cultivates a similar symbiosis in their music, where Southern folk traditions, New Orleans swamp culture, and Atlanta’s street spirit strengthen each other. Known for their seamless harmonies, songcatching and storytelling, the band has released ten albums and toured throughout North America, South America, Europe, the Celtic Isles, Australia and beyond — performing everywhere from the Telluride Bluegrass Festival and Red Rocks to NPR’s Tiny Desk. item.title: Visitor's Center to Folk Art Center — Fri Sep 11, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0 This is an easy to moderate hike, and we have a pace of about 30 to 3.2 mph. We take the Visitor's Center Loop to the Mountains to Sea Trail and turn around at the Folk Art Center. This hike is slightly over 5 miles. We should return between 11 and 11:10. There's is only one climb and it's on the way back, up some steps and a hill near Gashes Creek.
Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people. We stop at the 1/2 way point for a few minutes.

**What is Spirited Improv Playshop?**
A 2-hour playshop of movement, music, story, and unscripted connection. No script, no performance pressure, no experience needed. Just a circle of people willing to show up, play, and see what unfolds when a room lets go of the need to get it right.
**Who it's for** People craving real connection, creative expression, and a little more Love in their lives. If you're drawn to personal growth, spiritual community, or simply want an evening that feels different from the ones that came before it, this is for you.
**Led by** Jessica Chilton, an expressive arts practitioner and TEDx performer with twenty years in improvisational performing arts. She holds space with warmth and a deep trust in whatever wants to emerge in the room.

item.title: Southern Blue Ridge Fire Fair — Sat Sep 26, 9:00 AM — Myron Boon Hall
item.description: Do you have questions about fire in the Southern Blue Ridge Mountains? Join us on September 26th for the 3rd biannual Southern Blue Ridge Fire Fair, a free event for landowners, curious minds and prospective employees of fire and natural resources. We will hear from Adam Warwick, Stewardship Manager for The Nature Conservancy, on the role and importance of fire in our region. This will be followed by a networking event with local natural resource professionals to learn more about job opportunities, funding, technical assistance and other available resources. A free lunch will be provided, followed by a tour of a burn unit on the Warren Wilson College Forest with Dr. Armin Weise, Assistant Professor of Forest Management at Western Carolina University, and Juniper Odell, Prescribed Fire Specialist with the Nature Conservancy. item.title: Sober (Curious) Trivia Night! — Tue Sep 29, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Asheville Lose The Booze Crew (20-40s) Hi friends!! Let’s hang again at the Asheville Sports Club for a trivia night. You don't need to know it all (just hope that someone on your team does). 😆
**Trivia starts at 7:00 pm.** Arrive around 6:45 pm to establish teams. There is a 6-person maximum per team.
Asheville Sports Club has a slew of N/A options, please support our local business while you're impressing your trivia teammates with random knowledge about whales and NASCAR. 🧐
MISSION: We believe in equality, kindness and celebrating and encouraging others to explore their relationship with alcohol.
REMINDER: This is not a 12-step or recovery group, just folks that want to hang out sans booze, regardless of the reason.
DISCLAIMER: This is a public event. Asheville Sports Club serves alcohol. While you don't have to be sober to come to this event, we do ask that you refrain from drinking during our meet-up. Again, they do offer lots of N/A options, which is why we love them!!

item.title: Weekly Critique — Wed Sep 30, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).
Source: AVL Writers

item.description:
Carolina Craft Day October 3, 2026 10:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m. The Appalachian region has a rich history of crafts and art. Carolina Craft Day showcases traditional and contemporary crafts of our region. Purchase crafts from local artists and enjoy a drink from the Gardener’s Shed. Vendors and musicians will be stationed in the Heritage Garden and on Baker Lawn. Vendors: Pisgah Banjos Melanie Wilder (textiles and yarn dyeing; craft demos) WNC Wood (walking sticks and wood craft) Darcy Ward (metal work) Torched AVL (metalwork, jewelry, craft; craft demos) Trollgada (fishing lures) Skye Tafoya & Jakeli Swimmer (earrings, prints) Hannah Gambino (ceramics)

item.title: Guided Trail Walk — Sat Oct 3, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

item.title: Naturalist Walk and Talk - Spiders — Sat Oct 3, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Naturalist Walk and Talk – Spiders with Shane Myers Saturday, October 3 | 1 – 3pm BRN – Elective Register Here!
Walk around the Arboretum with our staff naturalists and talk about what we see around us. We might see plants and animals, and evidence of them going about their lives in our backyard. Topics will be based on what we see and experience and whatever questions that come up, so every class has the potential to be quite different. This month we will focus on the Spiders of the Arboretum. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio. item.title: Forest Bathing Retreat: The Experience of Fall — Sat Oct 3, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Forest Bathing Retreat: The Experience of Fall with Asheville Wellness Tours Saturday, October 3 | 2 – 5pm Register Here!
Join us for a celebration of autumn delights during this restorative afternoon nature connection retreat! From fall foliage to the monarch migration, we will immerse ourselves in the kaleidoscope that is autumn in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Enlivening our senses, calming our weary minds, and lingering in liminality. Together, we will discover natural pathways to equilibrium that will help us navigate life’s ups and downs, as well as the upcoming holiday season. Your guide, Kelly Bruce, will lead you on a colorful journey through the fall forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative afternoon on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. Happy hitting!

item.description:
With their very first note, Denmark’s Stundom captivates audiences with soaring melodies, irresistible rhythms, and a chemistry that has quickly made them rising stars on the European folk scene.
